superseded_runs.reason: CLI regression missed the parser declaration header; fixed before final verification. Other running matrices superseded.

production_source_comparison.interpretation: All 287 runtime/build paths match the tested cloud commit. Eight user extensions are retained; post-build documentation and original CCD loop failure-boundary research are separately recorded, not counted as part of cloud production verification.

limits: No real hardware setting, PBO effect or stability measurement has been verified.
Only Shimada family 1Ah/model 08h at PCI 1022:153a/BDF 0 is admitted for the new setting API.

Each selected core has fresh full-capability and identity checks. First failure stops later cores; accepted and attempted masks retain partial state. Frequency remains acknowledgement-only, with no physical mapping, retries, rollback or implicit OC/VID/scalar commands.
Fmax still has acknowledgement only. Rails has only an offline bounded encoding preview; physical targets and its two-command transaction remain unverified.
Original dynamic-memory and EC dynamic-EDC paths remain research-only. Their original Applied/return behavior is not proof of firmware acceptance or effective hardware changes.
Per-core/CCD PM telemetry layout remains unresolved. Other AMD profiles, native PM transport, Intel server controls and board-specific settings remain incomplete.
EL7 means Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64. Windows/macOS validate the portable core, not a full application port.
QEMU verifies module integration only; Secure Boot and actual register settings were not tested.

visual_review.method: Four PNGs opened with view_image and manually reviewed
observations: Selected target is explicitly firmware CCD 15 / cores 0,2,7. Requested 5000 MHz is separate from current-frequency readback, which is unavailable/not verified.

Completion table shows attempted/accepted masks 85, no stopped core and three firmware acknowledgements. The fixture then attempts another apply; the bottom message correctly requires a new capability read, and tests prove no extra command was sent.
Partial failure shows attempted mask 05, accepted mask 01 and stopped core 2. Core 0 is accepted, core 2 attempted/not confirmed with FD response, and core 7 not sent.
Partial-failure status says partial changes may remain, no automatic retry, and read capability again. Current frequency and physical mapping are not presented as verified.
Requested manual OC mode remains a separate desired-mode control; its Disabled selection is not a current-mode indicator and is not applied by the frequency action.
Result rows and status text are visible at 1400x1300 on both targets. Existing action labels use ellipsis; review covers these four result pages, not full-application layout.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; no real firmware acknowledgement, physical mapping or measured frequency.
The other 1338 desktop PNGs were archived but not individually viewed in this batch.

original_replay.scope: Original per-CCD wrapper and helper instructions. One Wr_SMU_arg command-write boundary per run returns a selected synthetic value; all other command writes return one. This is not an emulated firmware response or proof of a real I/O failure.

observations: REA normal amd_per_ccd_vermeer and fast per_ccx_freq_vermeer_fast expose fixed eight-core loops; normal writes six arguments and fast only argument zero.

768 original-instruction runs vary both wrappers, 16 CCD indices, eight command-write positions and three synthetic return values. Both wrappers continue all eight writes. This is not a real firmware rejection or failure of a real bus.
REA per_ccx_freq and fast wrappers have older four-core/CCX routing and modern eight-core routing selected by original globals. These globals are not new-platform hardware identity evidence.
REA single-core helpers confirm division by eight mixed with remainder modulo seven; do not infer physical mapping from flat original indices.

REA Qt caller implicitly enables OC and selects a voltage before the frequency loop, then reports Settings Applied without per-core acknowledgement checks. The new operation has no such implicit settings.

Pinned public Cpu.cs SetFrequencyMultipleCores stops when a single command fails, but assumes a count supplied by CCX helpers. New code requires an explicit list and compares full capabilities before each selected core.

New API supports Shimada 1Ah/08h and explicit CCD/core firmware encoding only, stops on first error and preserves partial acknowledgements. Frequency telemetry, active-core discovery, physical mapping and hardware acceptance remain unavailable.
